2609.35233.title: EP-Mem: Elastic Privacy Memory for Social Relationship-Aware LLM Agents
2609.35233.paper_summary: Large language model (LLM) agents face critical privacy risks when acting as delegates in human-agent-human communication. To prevent such breaches, agents must understand users' social relationships and adhere to context-dependent social information disclosure boundaries. Current studies on agent memory privacy focus on instantaneous interactions, leaving the long-term relational disclosure problem unexplored. In this paper, we propose EP-Mem, an Elastic Privacy Memory architecture that reframes privacy as user-owned boundary control across social roles. EP-Mem introduces (1) token-level memory driven by user-configurable a privacy policy that stratifies persons and events, combining domain-level default circulation rules with fact-level whitelist/blacklist exceptions; and (2) a pluggable sidecar with a privacy engine that aligns disclosure controls with memory across summary, detail, and boundary granularities, enforced throughout generation, storage, and retrieval. We construct EP-Bench, to our knowledge the first long-term multi-party benchmark with cross-session correlated events for policy-conditioned relational disclosure. Experiments show that EP-Mem achieves 94.0% privacy classification accuracy, improves disclosure-permission judgment from 22% to 68%, and reduces privacy leakage by 75.6%, while maintaining retrieval performance and cross-benchmark generalization.
2609.35233.paper_summary_zh: 大型語言模型（LLM）代理在作為人類-代理-人類溝通的代表時面臨嚴重的隱私風險。<lb/>為了防止此類違規行為，代理必須了解用戶的社交關係並遵循依賴於上下文的社交信息披露邊界。<lb/>目前對代理記憶隱私的研究集中在瞬時互動上，未能探討長期關係披露的問題。<lb/>在本文中，我們提出了EP-Mem，一種彈性隱私記憶架構，將隱私重新定義為用戶擁有的跨社交角色的邊界控制。<lb/>EP-Mem引入了（1）由用戶可配置的隱私政策驅動的令牌級記憶，該政策對人員和事件進行分層，結合了領域級的默認循環規則與事實級的白名單/黑名單例外；以及（2）一個可插拔的側車，配備隱私引擎，將披露控制與記憶在摘要、細節和邊界粒度上對齊，並在生成、存儲和檢索過程中強制執行。<lb/>我們構建了EP-Bench，據我們所知，這是第一個具有跨會話相關事件的長期多方基準，用於政策條件的關係披露。<lb/>實驗表明，EP-Mem達到了94.0%的隱私分類準確率，將披露許可判斷從22%提高到68%，並將隱私洩漏減少了75.6%，同時保持檢索性能和跨基準的泛化能力。
